plain_english_claim: Higher-education expansion is driven by globally legitimated models of the modern state (mass schooling as an attribute of statehood), so countries expand partly independently of their own economic demand.
functional_form: narrative-only. Literature reports a country-fixed-effects panel of expansion on national wealth, democratisation, science and world-society embeddedness, but the exact specification and coefficients were NOT retrieved. Form that would be needed: E_it = a_i + d_t + b1*ln(GDPpc)_it + b2*democr_it + b3*science_it + b4*WS_ties_it + e_it
variables_units: E = higher-education enrolment ratio (% of cohort); GDPpc = income per head (constant USD); democr = democracy index (unitless); science = science/S&T activity proxy (unitless); WS_ties = count of INGO/IO memberships per country (count)
parameters: a_i country FE; d_t year FE; b1..b4 NOT retrieved (no value available in this package); no prior value supplied
data_needed: cross-country HE enrolment panel + INGO/IO membership counts + democracy index + science proxy; none of these is on disk as a panel for the 6 countries
predicts: HE enrolment ratio; cross-national synchrony of expansion; expansion in low-return economies
programme_implementation: none (no code implements the world-society rival)
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: States adopt the *form* of mass schooling (a law, a ministry, a global target) long before capacity and completion follow; decoupling between adoption and outcome is the expected pattern, not a puzzle.
functional_form: narrative-only. Needs a two-equation adoption/outcome system: adopt_t = f(global declaration dates, IO ties); completion_t = g(capacity_t, adopt_{t-k}) with a long lag. No functional form is given in the literature.
variables_units: adopt_t = 0/1 adoption of the global model (law/ministry/target); completion_t = cohort completion (%); capacity_t = delivery capacity index (0-1, see SB-02); k = lag in years
parameters: lag k NOT estimated; no coefficient available
data_needed: coded adoption dates (EFA 1990, MDG 2 2000, SDG 4 2015, RA 10533 2013) + a justification corpus 2000-2013 (NOT on disk)
predicts: law adoption leading completion by long lags; adoption clustered after global declarations rather than after domestic return shocks
programme_implementation: none as an equation; used only as a timing narrative in RIVAL_MODELS_ANCHOR §2.1
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: One extra year of schooling raises a worker's earnings by about 8.8 per cent, other things equal; that wage premium is the price that pulls families into schooling.
functional_form: ln Y = alpha + r*S + b1*X + b2*X^2 + epsilon   (canonical Mincer earnings function)
variables_units: Y = annual earnings (local currency or PPP USD); S = years of schooling (years); X = potential experience (years); alpha = intercept; r = private return to one year of schooling (fraction/yr); b1,b2 = experience-profile coefficients; epsilon = error
parameters: r = 0.088 (world average, headline 'about 9%'); r = 0.087 (East Asia & Pacific); social return EAP = 0.069, >10% at secondary+ ; b1,b2 not needed for the register (Mincer compilation)
data_needed: country-level Mincer estimates by level and year (country annex of WPS8402; PSA FIES/APIS + LFS for PHL - DATA BLOCKED); no earnings microdata in any on-disk panel
predicts: earnings by schooling level; the return series that the demand-led rival says should lead enrolment
programme_implementation: NOT implemented as an equation: pushpull.py has no returns or earnings channel at all; 8.8% appears only as a calibration note
status: equation-in-literature

plain_english_claim: Families keep a child in school until the marginal private return on the extra year equals its marginal cost, counting the wages the child gives up while studying.
functional_form: narrative-only optimality condition (no estimable form given in the reviewed layer): continue iff r_t * PV(earnings gain from the extra year) >= MC_t, where MC_t includes direct fees + foregone earnings.
variables_units: r_t = return to the marginal year (fraction/yr); PV = present value (currency); MC_t = marginal cost incl. foregone earnings (currency/yr)
parameters: no parameter value supplied by the literature for our countries; the condition is qualitative
data_needed: time series of returns by level, direct costs, and opportunity cost (foregone earnings); none measured on disk for PHL
predicts: enrolment and continuation; deceleration of expansion when returns fall (the programme's motivating anomaly)
programme_implementation: none; pushpull.py has no cost, fee or foregone-earnings term (the 2016/2018 free-SHS/free-tertiary events enter only as 0/1 markers in anchor.py L77-79)
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: Expansion should follow expected returns with a lag, and should slow down when returns fall. This is the discriminating prediction that separates the human-capital story from the positional one.
functional_form: narrative-only. Form that would be needed: d(Enrol)_t / Enrol = c + a*dr_{t-k} + controls, i.e. a lagged elasticity of enrolment to the return series, estimated per level.
variables_units: Enrol = enrolment or completion rate (%); r = return to the level (fraction/yr); k = payoff-horizon lag (years); a = elasticity (unknown)
parameters: a and k: NOT FOUND. No retrieved source supplies a returns->enrolment elasticity for any of the six countries (SCALING_LAWS.md §3; ECON_TARGETS 'Enrolment-ratio elasticity to GDP p.c. - NOT FOUND, must estimate')
data_needed: a level-specific return series and a level-specific completion/enrolment series over the same years; the return series is BLOCKED (PSA 403)
predicts: lead-lag sign of returns -> enrolment; the deceleration test when returns fall
programme_implementation: none; the E3 nurse-visa cell that would have proxied it is predeclared but NOT RUN and DATA BLOCKED (model/PRE_EXP_E3_PH_NURSES.md)
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: An observably identical worker earns about four times as much in the United States as in the Philippines, so the payoff to a marketable credential is set by the destination labour market, not the home one.
functional_form: Place premium = ratio of the PPP wage of an observably identical worker abroad to the home wage, estimated from a Mincer regression with country dummies on pooled microdata (definition, not a structural equation).
variables_units: place premium = 3.99 (ratio, PPP wage); range 3.71-4.36; home/destination wages (PPP USD)
parameters: 3.99 (range 3.71-4.36), Clemens, Montenegro & Pritchett 2008 (WPS4671); 'TARGET' in ECON_TARGETS
data_needed: migration and wage microdata; destination credential-recognition rules (NOT on disk)
predicts: the price that a household responds to when foreign demand rises; predicts the origin-country training boom (9 licensed nurses per additional migrant)
programme_implementation: none; E3 predeclared only (model/PRE_EXP_E3_PH_NURSES.md), NOT RUN
status: equation-in-literature (definition + verified estimate)

plain_english_claim: Workers queue for jobs that are ranked by how much training they need, and schooling moves a worker up the queue. So schooling buys a position, not productivity.
functional_form: narrative-only. Literature states a labour queue ranked by background/training cost with the wage set by the job, not the worker: hire_i = P(rank_i, queue length); w_i = w(job). No closed form is reproduced.
variables_units: rank_i = queue position (ordinal); queue length (persons); w(job) = job-specific wage (currency); years of schooling (years)
parameters: no parameter value supplied (pure theory)
data_needed: employer requirement schedule / job postings by required credential; queue length or graduate-unemployment series. NEITHER exists on disk (ECON_TARGETS rows 'share of jobs formally requiring a degree' = unusable)
predicts: credential requirement ratcheting up while job content is flat; education expanding regardless of skill demand
programme_implementation: none as an equation; the queue rival is present only as prose in the rival tables (RIVAL_MODELS_ANCHOR §2.3)
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: Education mainly signals ability that was already there; firms pay for the signal, not the skill. Private returns can be positive while the social return is near zero.
functional_form: narrative-only in this layer ('signalling equilibrium conditions on cost-of-acquisition differences by type; screening model with test costs. Not reproduced here'). Form that would be needed: a separating equilibrium in which w(S) is increasing and the single-crossing condition c_S(S, theta_low) < c_S(S, theta_high) holds.
variables_units: S = schooling signal (years); theta = worker type/ability; c(S,theta) = cost of acquiring the signal (currency); w(S) = wage schedule (currency)
parameters: no parameter value; single-crossing condition is qualitative
data_needed: employer learning about productivity; returns surviving ability controls; test scores linked to earnings
predicts: defensive acquisition of the next tier as a signal saturates; returns that survive ability controls
programme_implementation: none
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: The admission line sits a fixed number of standard deviations above the cohort mean, so effort concentrates on the students just below that line.
functional_form: S_cut = S_bar + k * sigma_S ;  S_i = gamma_i * t_i ;  u_i = log(2 + S_i - S_cut) - C_i if S_i >= S_cut, else -C_i ;  C_i = P_i * t_i
variables_units: S_i = score (points); gamma_i = aptitude (points/hour); t_i = study time (hours); S_bar = mean score; sigma_S = score sd; S_cut = admission line; k = line width in sd (unitless); C_i = cost (currency); P_i = price of study time
parameters: k ~ 1.645 corresponds to the 5th percentile (the paper's own example). No estimated value for PHL/KOR; the paper has no data and no calibration.
data_needed: score distribution and study-time data by cohort; not on disk in any form
predicts: the gate position; effort concentrated near S_bar + k*sigma; the tournament share of investment
programme_implementation: none (this is a gate rule, not used in pushpull.py; the programme's gate is a capacity index, not a score line)
status: equation-in-literature

plain_english_claim: Private tutoring is a contest for a fixed admission bar: students near the bar work hardest, and moving the bar to either extreme reduces total effort.
functional_form: T = alpha*e + epsilon ;  Prob(admit) = 1 - F(t* - alpha*e) = F(alpha*e - t*) ;  max_e  X*F(alpha*e - t*) - beta*c(e) ;  FOC: X*f(alpha*e - t*)*alpha = beta*c'(e)
variables_units: T = test score (points); e = tutoring purchased (hours or units); alpha = score return to effort (points/unit); epsilon = mean-zero shock with sd sigma; t* = the bar (points); X = valuation of the prize (currency); beta = marginal-cost shifter (currency); c(e) convex cost
parameters: alpha, beta, t*, X, sigma: no empirical values (pure theory, no calibration); f symmetric, c'(0)=0, c''>0 imposed
data_needed: score distributions, tutoring expenditure, admission cutoffs; not on disk
predicts: effort peaks near the gate; aggregate rent seeking rises when the cut-off sits mid-distribution and falls at the extremes
programme_implementation: none
status: equation-in-literature

plain_english_claim: With two families competing for one place, paying for tutoring becomes the dominant strategy as soon as the prize is worth more than twice the cost - a prisoner's dilemma that no family can escape alone.
functional_form: EW = P*W + (1-P)*0 - C ; contest technology: if one parent pays C and the other pays 0, the payer's child is admitted with probability 1; if both pay, each has probability 0.5. If W > 2C then (PT, PT) is a dominant-strategy Nash equilibrium and is Pareto-inferior.
variables_units: EW = expected payoff (currency); P = admission probability; W = value of the prize (currency); C = cost of tutoring (currency)
parameters: threshold W > 2C (a condition, not a calibrated value); no empirical estimate
data_needed: household tutoring expenditure and admission probabilities; not on disk
predicts: defensive investment whenever the prize exceeds twice the cost; an equilibrium with no tutoring when W < 2C
programme_implementation: none
status: equation-in-literature
citation: Kim 2007, NCSPE OP144, eq 3 and Table 2

plain_english_claim: When a level of schooling expands, richer families fill it first; inequality in the chance of moving up a level only falls once the rich have saturated it. Expansion alone does not equalise.
functional_form: narrative-only. The object is a matrix of class-specific conditional transition probabilities P(transition | origin class, level) with inequality read as odds ratios across origins. No closed-form law is given.
variables_units: P = transition probability (0-1); origin class (categorical); level (primary/lower/upper/tertiary); odds ratio (unitless)
parameters: no parameter value; the claim is qualitative ('inequality falls after saturation')
data_needed: class-specific completion or transition data from household surveys (PSA/CLS); BLOCKED for PHL
predicts: the timing of gradient narrowing relative to saturation; a benchmark the programme's 'floor' mechanism must beat
programme_implementation: none; MMI is listed as design-only in every results table (STATUS.md D48)
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: Families continue schooling to avoid dropping down the class ladder. Because what is being defended is relative position, the class gap survives even when fees fall.
functional_form: narrative-only. Expected-utility comparison over class destinations with a relative-risk-aversion parameter: choose continue iff E[U(class | continue)] - E[U(class | stop)] > 0, with U exhibiting relative risk aversion.
variables_units: class destinations (categorical); U = utility over class position; RRA coefficient (unitless)
parameters: RRA coefficient: canonical object, original value NOT read in this layer
data_needed: household class origin and transition choices; not on disk
predicts: the gradient persisting while absolute costs fall; compression of the gradient only when continuing becomes the low-risk option for all classes
programme_implementation: none
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: Credentials are a way for status groups to close ranks. Supply expands, the credential inflates, and the required credential ratchets up while the job itself is unchanged.
functional_form: narrative-only. Form that would be needed is a ratchet rule: requirement_t = requirement_{t-1} + g*(supply of credential-holders_t - demand_t), with g > 0 - i.e. the requirement chases relative supply, not job content.
variables_units: requirement_t = credential required for a job (categorical/ordinal); supply of holders (persons); g = ratchet speed (unknown)
parameters: g: NOT FOUND; ECON_TARGETS 'causal effect of credential requirements on hiring' = unusable
data_needed: employer requirement series / job postings, or a credential module in Enterprise Surveys; not on disk
predicts: the required credential rising independent of job content; returns stable while supply doubles (the falsifier)
programme_implementation: none
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: When too many degrees are produced, graduates cascade down into jobs below their level and push everyone else down; universities make it worse by hiring their own unmatched graduates, which produces more graduates.
functional_form: narrative-only at equation level (the equations live in a Vensim appendix and were not individually readable). Verified structure: three workforce stocks W1<W2<W3 matched to three job tiers J1<J2<J3 top-down, nobody may take a job above their own education; two education stages S2,S3 with a delay; TPA inflow = r * unmatched W3.
variables_units: W1..W3 = workforce by credential (persons); J1..J3 = jobs by required level (persons); S2,S3 = student stocks; r = share of unmatched graduates hired into temporary academic posts (0-1); delay = degree-production lag (years)
parameters: r: no value (the authors state the parameters are explicitly hypothetical); baseline 1000 persons/jobs per tier
data_needed: credential stocks, job tiers, provider capacity; not on disk
predicts: degree supply overshooting job demand after a shock; underemployment of the most educated; a U-shaped provider-feedback effect
programme_implementation: none; the model is cited as a shape prediction only (RIVAL_MODELS_ANCHOR §2.6)
status: narrative-only (structure verified; equations unreadable)

plain_english_claim: A schooling law only moves enrolment to the extent the state can actually deliver and enforce it: the effect of a legal marker is the marker multiplied by a capacity gate that runs from 0 to 1.
functional_form: effective_push_t = law_t * G(C_t) ;  G(C) = C^kappa, with kappa = 0.75 (declared range 0.5-1.0) ;  push enters additively on transition probabilities: p_pri += push_floor, p_low += push_floor, p_up += push_ceiling, p_ter += push_ceiling, with push_floor = PUSH*law*G(C) and push_ceiling = CEIL*PUSH*law*G(C)
variables_units: effective_push_t = additive change to a transition probability (probability points); law_t = 0/1 policy marker; C_t = capacity index in [0,1]; kappa = gate exponent (unitless); PUSH = 0.05 (declared additive scale); CEIL = 0.25 (declared saturating share for upper/tertiary)
parameters: kappa = 0.75 (declared default; declared range [0.5,1.0]; sensitivity over kappa DECLARED BUT NEVER RUN - audit D-07); PUSH = 0.05; CEIL = 0.25; all programme-declared, none from the literature
data_needed: law dates (policy timeline) + capacity inputs (see SB-02); both on disk for PHL
predicts: the timing of completion crossings; the floor levels responding more than the ceiling levels
programme_implementation: model/anchor.py L64-90 (gate, arms); model/pushpull.py L104-113 (push applied); kappa at anchor.py L64
status: programme-invented (the Council declared the functional form in A9/A10; the literature supplies only the qualitative claim that laws bind where enforced)
citation: Paglayan 2024; Gellner 1983; Tilly 1990 (mechanism only); Council A9/A10 (form)

plain_english_claim: State capacity is measured as a weighted mix of three things: how many pupils each teacher carries (delivery), how much of national income goes to education (fiscal), and how many years of school are legally required (enforcement).
functional_form: C_t = sum_j w_j * x_jt with w = (delivery 0.5, fiscal 0.3, enforcement 0.2);  x_delivery = clip((40 - PTR)/20, 0, 1);  x_fiscal = clip((pctGDP - 2)/3, 0, 1);  x_enforcement = compulsory_years/13 ; missing input -> its weight is dropped and the rest renormalised; flat back-fill before the first observation
variables_units: C_t = capacity index [0,1]; PTR = pupil-teacher ratio (pupils per teacher); pctGDP = government education spending (% of GDP); compulsory_years = legal compulsory duration (years); w_j = declared weights (0.5/0.3/0.2)
parameters: weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 (declared); PTR map 40->0, 20->1; spending map 2%->0, 5%->1; compulsory years 6 / 10 / 13 (pre-1987 / 1987-2012 / 2013+). Resulting PHL series: C(1960)=0.2337, C(1990)=0.2952, C(2017)=0.7964, C(2024)=0.7925 (anchor_out/run_meta.json)
data_needed: PTR path (PHL high-school PTR 37 (2000) -> 27 (2014) -> 24 (2017)); education spending %GDP; compulsory duration from POLICY_TIMELINE.csv
predicts: the capacity gate input C_t; the capacity-timing test
programme_implementation: model/anchor.py L46-61 (index), L34-43 (interpolation/back-fill); committed values in model/anchor_out/run_meta.json
status: programme-invented (weights and rescaling are declared assumptions, not estimates)
citation: Council A9 §1-2 (programme decision); no literature source for the weights

plain_english_claim: A compulsory-schooling law is necessary but not sufficient. What binds is delivery (places, teachers) plus enforcement, and in low-capacity states attendance laws are widely treated as non-binding.
functional_form: narrative-only. Form that would be needed: attendance_effective = law_t * e_t, where e_t in [0,1] is a measured enforcement intensity (inspection, sanctions, conditional cash transfers), not a de jure duration.
variables_units: law_t = 0/1 compulsion; e_t = enforcement intensity (0-1); attendance/completion (% of cohort)
parameters: no enforcement parameter is measurable in this package: 'there is no observed enforcement-capacity series' (STATE_CAPACITY.md §1.4); the programme substitutes compulsory duration/13, which is a de jure proxy and is double-counted inside G(C) (audit D-09)
data_needed: attendance/inspection/sanction series or LGU monitoring data; DATA BLOCKED (zero enforcement data in the package)
predicts: whether completion jumps where enforcement is credible; the falsifier 'a law with no enforcement producing universal completion'
programme_implementation: no enforcement equation exists; anchor.py L58 uses compulsory duration as a de jure proxy inside C_t
status: narrative-only

plain_english_claim: The number of children born each year is set by how many women of childbearing age there are and by the fertility rate; that birth cohort becomes the school intake six years later.
functional_form: births_t = 0.5 * sum_{a=15..49} pop_{a,t-1} * TFR_t / 35 ;  pop_{0,t} = births_t
variables_units: births_t = births in year t (persons); pop_a = population at age a (persons); TFR = total fertility rate (births per woman); the 0.5 is the assumed female share, 35 the assumed childbearing span (years)
parameters: female share 0.5 (declared); childbearing span 15-49 / 35 years (declared); TFR paths: PHL 4.32(1990)->3.75(2000)->3.31(2010)->2.08(2020) S; KHM 5.64->3.79->2.86->2.70 S; HKG 1.27->1.03->1.13->0.88 S; CHN 2.51->1.63->1.69->1.24 S; KOR and JPN A (assumed, WDI not on disk)
data_needed: annual TFR series per country (WDI SP.DYN.TFRT.IN); on disk for 4 of 6 countries only
predicts: the size of the school-age cohort and hence per-child schooling cost and GER denominators
programme_implementation: model/pushpull.py L71-74; TFR paths in model/configs.py L14-21
status: programme-invented (a declared demographic approximation; no source equation)
citation: no citation (demographic accounting convention, declared as assumption 'A' in configs.py)

plain_english_claim: People age one year at a time and a fixed share of each age band survives each year; nobody is modelled individually.
functional_form: pop_{a,t} = pop_{a-1,t-1} * s_a, with s = {0.995 for age<5, 0.994 for 5<=age<60, 0.96 for age>=60}
variables_units: pop_a = population at age a (persons); s_a = annual survival probability by age band (unitless)
parameters: s = 0.995 / 0.994 / 0.96 (declared constant age-band survival; labelled 'A: constant age-band survival (declared approximation)')
data_needed: country life tables (not on disk for this purpose)
predicts: the age structure, hence the denominator of every GER
programme_implementation: model/pushpull.py L36-39 (survival) and L75-77 (ageing); model/configs.py L41
status: programme-invented (declared approximation; three-band constant survival, no country life table)

plain_english_claim: Larger cohorts dilute per-child resources and depress completion: the higher the fertility rate, the lower primary completion, both across countries and within a country over time.
functional_form: semi-log relation as estimated: completion_primary on ln(TFR) (the register records only the label 'semi-log'; the exact link - level vs logit - is not stated in the CSV, which is a recorded ambiguity). Coefficients: within -0.1893 (se 0.0436, t=-4.34, n=712, 28 countries); between -0.1222 (se 0.0267, t=-4.57)
variables_units: completion_primary = primary completion rate (% of cohort); TFR = total fertility rate (births per woman); coefficient = semi-elasticity (pp per log unit, sign negative)
parameters: within -0.1893 (se 0.0436); between -0.1222 (se 0.0267); FE: country+year / year only; all graded 'correlational'
data_needed: completion by level and TFR/population, both on disk (30-country panel; UIS6)
predicts: primary completion; the cohort-size channel that Z4 is predeclared to test as a lagged cohort shock
programme_implementation: relations/data/scaling_laws.csv rows S12-within/S12-between (estimated in 10_massification/relations/; no model channel consumes it)
status: programme-estimated (the underlying hypothesis is graded NOT VERIFIED in the literature layer; the coefficient is the programme's own estimate)
citation: no literature estimate (SCALING_LAWS §6: cohort-size effect NOT VERIFIED); estimate is programme-side

plain_english_claim: Universalization always arrives in the same order - primary, then lower secondary, then upper secondary, then tertiary - with the gaps between the steps widening as you go up.
functional_form: narrative-only as an equation; the object is a vector of crossing years and the gaps between consecutive elements. Needed form: t_cross(level) = f(level) with t_cross increasing and gaps g_level = t_cross(level+1) - t_cross(level) increasing.
variables_units: t_cross = first year a level crosses its threshold (year); g = gap between crossings (years); measure must be named (GER vs NER vs completion differ by up to a decade)
parameters: PHL observed: primary completion >=90 in 2017; lower-secondary >=90 in 2024; upper-secondary never >=90 by 2024 (75.03); tertiary GER >=50 in the 2024-25 band. Tolerance +/-5 y (+/-3 y narrow). N=3 dated systems only (X6 UNABLE)
data_needed: completion series by level for each country; available for PHL, CHN, KHM; KOR partial; JPN/HKG completion NOT FOUND
predicts: the ordering and spacing of crossings - the programme's declared discriminating outcome (A6)
programme_implementation: no code implements this as an equation; scored as a vector in model/anchor.py L147-150 and model2/code/e6.py
status: narrative-only (an observed regularity, not a literature equation; the spacing is the target, not a fitted curve)

plain_english_claim: Intake at age six rises when jobs were plentiful a few years earlier (the demand-pull channel), and is capped so it can never exceed 100 per cent of the cohort.
functional_form: intake_t = clip( intake_{t-1} * [ 1 + 0.1 * e_d * (job_{t-lag_d} / job_t - 1) ], 0.2, 1.0 )
variables_units: intake_t = share of the age-6 cohort entering school (0-1); job = job-opportunities index (unitless); e_d = jobs->schooling elasticity; lag_d = lag in years; 0.1 = declared damping constant
parameters: e_d in [0, 0.6] (calibrate.py BOUNDS) but [0, 0.8] in configs.py CHANNEL_PRIORS - the two declared ranges DISAGREE; lag_d in [0, 3] (calibrate.py) vs [0, 5] (configs.py) - also disagreeing; damping 0.1 declared
data_needed: lagged formal-job or wage-share series; the model uses its own job index, not an observed series
predicts: the intake rate and hence every enrolment stock
programme_implementation: model/pushpull.py L83-84; bounds at model/calibrate.py BOUNDS and model/configs.py CHANNEL_PRIORS
status: programme-invented (the form - a damped ratio of lagged to current job opportunities - is not in any cited literature)
citation: none (programme design; PREDECLARATION.md declares the channel only qualitatively)

plain_english_claim: The chance of moving up from one school level to the next rises with national income and with urbanisation, and (in the demand-led version) with job opportunities.
functional_form: p_k = clip( a_k + g_k*ln(gdp) + u_k*urb + m_k*ln(gdp) [ + 0.02*e_d*ln(job) ], lo_k, hi_k ) for k in {primary, lower, upper, tertiary}
variables_units: p_k = annual progression probability (0-1); gdp = income index (unitless, 1.0 at 1960); urb = urban population share (0-1); job = job-opportunities index; a_k = intercept; g_k,u_k,m_k = slopes; lo_k/hi_k = declared clips (0.3/0.995, 0.2/0.99, 0.1/0.98, 0.02/0.95)
parameters: intercepts a_k and slopes g_k,u_k are the FREE fitted parameters (14 in calibrate.KEYS with declared bounds); clip bounds and the 0.02 damping are declared; note the code is a CLIPPED LINEAR function, while the predeclaration describes it as 'logistic(...)' (PRE_SCALING_REPAIR.md §2) - a code/text divergence
data_needed: income and urbanisation series per country (on disk, WDI); job series (model-generated)
predicts: completion at each level (as the product of the p's) and the enrolment stocks
programme_implementation: model/pushpull.py L95-103 (progression); L130-136 (completion products); model/calibrate.py KEYS
status: programme-invented (a declared reduced form; not taken from any cited equation)

plain_english_claim: Job opportunities grow exogenously over time and faster when the workforce is better educated - this is the supply-push feedback from schooling to jobs.
functional_form: job_opp_t = exp( 0.012 * (t - 1960) ) * ( 1 + e_s * (educ_share - 0.15) )
variables_units: job_opp = job-opportunities index (unitless); t = year; educ_share = educated share of the labour force (0-1); e_s = education->jobs elasticity; 0.012 = declared autonomous growth rate (per year); 0.15 = declared baseline educated share
parameters: e_s in [0, 0.6]; 0.012 per year and the 0.15 baseline are declared; no literature value
data_needed: formal-sector job growth / wage-and-salaried share series; the model uses its own index
predicts: job opportunities, which then feed intake (PP-01) and GDP growth (PP-04)
programme_implementation: model/pushpull.py L79
status: programme-invented

Only 68 of 194 series are identified; where a series starts at the ceiling the midpoint is pinned at the bound and must not be quoted.
